newsitem.title: USA: Mexico's Avantel sees breakeven in 3 to 5 years.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Avantel sees breakeven in 3 to 5 years.

text.p: Mexican telephone company Avantel, a joint venture between MCI Communications Corp and Mexico's Grupo Financiero Banamex Accival SA de CV, should reach a breakeven point in three to five years, a senior company executive said on Tuesday.

Daniel Crawford, the company's chief operating officer and president, told a Salomon Brother's telecommunications conference that Avantel's goal was 20 percent of the Mexican long-distance market in five to seven years.
He said Avantel had completed 3,200 miles (5,400 km) of telecommunications systems since receiving a government license in September 1995.

Avantel, 45 percent owned by MCI, is among several company's competing for a piece of Mexico's rapidly liberalizing telecommunications market. The company will invest $900 million by the end of 1997. "We want cash flow and earnings to break even in three to five years," he said.
He would not speculate on Avantel's revenues for 1996 nor 1997, saying investment so far had focused on construction rather than marketing or sales.
He added that the returns would depend in part on the speed at which the market opens.
The Mexican government has scheduled the opening's first stage to begin gradually on January 1, with about 60 percent of the market to be open to competition by mid-year.
